## TL;DR

Test helpers — fake CLIs, preview servers and `bun -e` stubs — survived the run that spawned them because cleanup lived only in per-test `try/finally` blocks, which a worker kill or check timeout never reaches. `global-reap` could only kill pids recorded in `spawns.log`, and it scanned the inherited `TMPDIR`, which in managed agent runs points inside the checkout rather than at the OS temp dir where the run root lives. Every run left helpers behind, and the next run never looked where they were.

The fix has four layers: a shared `spawnTestProcess()` helper that starts a helper in its own group and records it, a per-test-file hook that kills those groups after every test, a global teardown that kills any process whose command line names the run's unique temp root (and fails the run if anything survives SIGKILL), and — phase 2 — a slow control-plane census that reaps orphans even when the whole test process was killed. Matching is always by the run-scoped path or `REPOOS_TEST_HELPER` tag, never by process name.

## Work and rationale

`src/ui-app/tests/helpers.ts` gained process primitives: `listProcessEntries()`, `terminateTestPidsSync()` (SIGTERM, wait, SIGKILL, ignore zombies), and `findProcessesMatchingRoots()` with a path-boundary check so `/tmp/repoos-vitest-Abc` does not match `/tmp/repoos-vitest-Abc2`. Only a process that leads its own group is signalled with `-pid`, and the current process group is always excluded.

`spawnTestProcess()` spawns detached on POSIX, records the pid in `$REPOOS_TEST_TMP_ROOT/test-processes.jsonl`, and puts it in a worker-local set. `tests/setup/process-guard.ts` drains that set in `afterEach` and `afterAll`, so a failed assertion or timeout cannot leak before global teardown.

`global-reap` teardown collects recorded pids, matches command lines against the run root, terminates, and throws a `[global-reap] test helper process(es) survived teardown` error if anything remains. Setup calls `sweepOrphanedRunRootProcesses()` for helpers whose root no longer exists, then reaps stale fixture dirs. `reapStaleFixtures()` scans both the inherited temp dir and the real OS temp dir, and kills recorded pids plus command-line matches before deleting paths: once a directory is gone, the command line is the only record left.

Phase 2 adds the machine-wide safety net in `src/server/system.ts`. `scanTestHelperProcesses()` walks `ps` once, then probes cwd (`lsof`) and the env tag only for cheap-gate candidates. `classifyTestHelperProcess()` requires same uid, `ppid` 1, age over 30 minutes, a RepoOS test temp dir in command/cwd/tag, no live owning run, and no path inside a task worktree. `reapLeakedTestHelpers()` SIGTERMs the process group, waits 1.5 s, then SIGKILLs survivors. `server.ts` arms it on the control plane only, three minutes after boot and every 12 minutes, logging each reap.

## Approaches tried

The first attempt relied on existing `spawns.log` pid records; it missed preview servers and `bun -e` stubs that never write one, and still scanned the wrong temp dir. A second attempt checked survivors with `process.kill(pid, 0)`, which reports success for a zombie, so the guard failed correctly cleaned runs. Zombies are now excluded (`<defunct>`). The orphan sweep also became age-gated so a concurrent run in another checkout is untouched.

## Challenges and blockers

No human blocker. The main subtlety was distinguishing "dead" from "zombie" and avoiding numeric process-group collisions; both are covered by the new leak-guard test. The scoped check delegated tests to remote validation, so I also ran `bun run test -- --changed main` locally: 659 files / 8600 tests passed, plus the isolated boot-timing pass, and `ps` showed zero remaining helpers afterwards.

## Key learnings

Leak cleanup has to survive the path where no user code runs. A pid log is not enough when its directory is deleted; a run-scoped path in the command line is the durable handle, and matching it is safe because it is unique per run. The guard only works if it treats zombies as dead and checks both temp dirs.
